The project README gives the overview. Oriel is a developer preview, with local execution and explicit review. Authored sample definitions let you explore briefs without a model, simulator or registry account. Context-agent bootstrap and questions use the configured model with consent.

The latest tested revision passes 52 local cases and four configured-model cases across both synthetic profiles before and after refresh. Live-vendor validation and clean Git/public-checkout reproduction remain pending. The evidence record distinguishes current working-tree installation checks from committed and published source proof.

Work through a complete example

Start with the Customer 360 application. Billing/support and CRM/conversation samples use the same interface. Load data, review identities and mappings, bootstrap and approve context, inspect a customer brief, then save and compare it after refresh. Goal and verification separates deterministic, actual model and live-vendor evidence.

The earlier CRM seats and product activity recipe remains a useful advanced CLI example. It shows identity review, metric reuse by a separate consumer and changed-data calculations. Its fixtures and independent expected-answer code are in examples/tool-exports.

The payments and unresolved issues example is a separate synthetic recipe. Its recorded capture can run offline; running the simulator itself has additional requirements. Neither recipe establishes performance advantages over another architecture.
